heard: Before their civilization collapsed, the Nazca cut down their own desert defense. Intricate geoglyphs of animals stretched across more than 1,300 kilometers of dry plateau. Expanding agriculture drove them to clear the deep-rooted Waranggu trees. An El Nino event around 500 AD unleashed torrential coastal flooding. Without root systems, the unprotected soil washed away into deep river channels. Floods destroyed their canals, leaving future generations to wonder why the Nazca destroyed their own ecosystem.
